text:
maya: heads up — running into a weird duplication of request IDs in the node sampleapp when retry middleware kicks in. logs show two x-redwood-reqid headers sometimes.
ben: ugh, that sounds bad. can you paste a short repro?
maya: minimal case attached inline. express app with our reqid middleware + otel auto-hook + retry proxy. sometimes the outgoing retry attaches another reqid header instead of preserving the original.
sam: is this the fetch-retry lib we added last sprint? it mutates headers on retry if a header-modifier is present.
maya: yep. code: ```js
// simplified middleware order in app.js
app.use(require('./middleware/reqid')) // sets req.xReqId = uuid() and res.set('x-redwood-reqid', id)
app.use(require('@opentelemetry/instrumentation-express').middleware()) // OTEL context propagation
app.use(require('./middleware/retry-proxy')) // forwards to model service with fetch-retry
```
maya: when retry-proxy does the second attempt, fetch-retry calls: `headers.append('x-redwood-reqid', generatedId)` instead of preserving the existing header. logs then show `x-redwood-reqid: a1b2..,a1b2..` which breaks our log parser.
ben: does fetch-retry append or set? append would create a comma-separated header on node's Headers.
eli: Node http headers are case-insensitive but if you call `res.setHeader('x-redwood-reqid', [orig, new])` you'll end up with comma list. our loghook treats comma as separate reqids and then redaction/deduping fails.
maya: exact. sample log: `INFO request handler req_id=a1b2c3 span=... outgoing_headers=x-redwood-reqid=a1b2c3,a1b2c3`
sam: ok. two separate problems: (1) retry lib should preserve headers or do a `set` not `append`. (2) our otel/reqid hook ordering might be wrong so the first attempt doesn't get proper traceparent sometimes.
ben: quick check: what's the hook order in the Node SDK? we intended reqid -> otel -> loghook so logs always include reqid and trace info.
maya: currently we initialize OTEL instrumentation in the SDK init which runs *after* express middlewares in our sampleapp because the starter script requires `./server` before `./telemetry/init.js`. feels brittle.
eli: that's a problem. if telemetry init runs late, the otel instrumentation might register duplicate hooks or miss ctx on retries.
maya: repro steps I used: start sampleapp locally, call /generate (which proxies) with `ab -n 2 -c 1` and toggle `RETRY_ATTEMPT=1` to force retry. logs attached.
infra-bot: deploy-trigger:repro-job queued (job/telemetry/repro-2087654321).
sam: thanks infra-bot. temporary mitigation: change retry-proxy to `if (headers.get('x-redwood-reqid')) { headers.set('x-redwood-reqid', headers.get('x-redwood-reqid')) } else { headers.set('x-redwood-reqid', id) }` — essentially ensure `.set` not `.append`.
ben: agree. also we should add header dedupe in the loghook: split on commas and pick first non-empty token as canonical reqid, then redact extras. that prevents parsing chaos if other libs append.
maya: I implemented a tiny patch locally to dedupe and it made logs sane: `const canonical = hdr.split(',')[0].trim()` -> works.
eli: long-term we should update Node SDK docs to mandate telemetry init before server start (or export an init function to call from server start). Also add a check in `@redwood/sdk` to warn if instrumentation initialized after server listening.
sam: and add unit test: simulate header with two ids and ensure loghook extracts first. add e2e that runs sampleapp with fetch-retry and asserts single reqid in logs.
ben: can you open a PR, maya? tag it `devex/telemetry-reqid-retry-fix` and include: repro, patch to retry-proxy (set vs append), loghook dedupe, docs note.
maya: yep will open PR in ~2h. assigning tasks: maya -> PR + repro, ben -> review + add SDK warning, sam -> add e2e, eli -> telemetry docs patch. target: ship patch in next minor (0.12.1).
eli: also add a changelog note for customers migrating from older fetch libraries.
maya: one more edge-case: if someone intentionally sends multiple reqids (for multi-hop tracing) our dedupe could drop info. should we parse first as canonical but preserve list in `meta.raw_reqids`?
ben: good call — keep canonical for indexing and stash raw header into debug meta (redacted). that stays internal only.
sam: I'll update tests to assert raw preserved.
maya: thanks team. I'll paste the repro logs & stack trace in the PR.
ben: :thumbsup: appreciate the quick triage.
